title: Length of the Tseitin Clause Chain
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $L$ and $A$ be lists of literals on $n$ coordinates. If the length of $L$ is at most the length of $A$ plus $3$, then the number of clauses in their Tseitin clause chain is $\max(|L|-2,1)$, where $|L|$ denotes the length of $L$.
